summary:
The Fire Risk Detector is a web application powered by a Python-based FastAPI backend and a Dart-based frontend. It monitors active thermal anomalies and estimates fire risks in real-time by leveraging satellite imagery and live environmental data. I built a FastAPI backend that retrieves real-time VIIRS and MODIS data from NASA FIRMS, correlates hotspots within a 1.0 km radius and a 3600-second time window, applies a 1.25x calibration factor to the MODIS FRP (Fire Radiative Power), and generates fire predictions. For the frontend, I developed a Flutter web interface featuring interactive map layers, historical fire data, and automated, location-based risk insights. The application consolidates fragmented VIIRS and MODIS data into a unified, consistent dataset of hotspots, integrating active thermal monitoring with environmental risk factors—all within an intuitive, browser-based workflow.
Why this matters: An early, unified view of fire risks supports faster awareness, clearer comparisons of severity, and practical decision-making.
details:
Fire Risk Detector is a web application built to monitor active thermal anomalies and estimate wildfire risk in near-real time by combining live satellite observations with environmental data. Rather than treating fire monitoring as a purely reactive process after a fire has already grown large, the system brings together a Python FastAPI backend and a Dart/Flutter web frontend to give users clear, accessible insights directly in the browser.
#### Backend Architecture & Multi-Sensor Harmonization
At the core of the backend is a FastAPI service that pulls near-real-time thermal anomaly feeds from NASA FIRMS, specifically integrating detections from both VIIRS and MODIS. Because these two sensors differ in spatial resolution, observation timing, and how they measure heat intensity, raw data from each source can appear fragmented or inconsistent when viewed side by side.
To address this, the backend performs multi-sensor harmonization across three main stages:
* Spatial and Temporal Correlation: Hotspot detections from VIIRS and MODIS are matched when they occur within a 1.0 km radius and a 3600-second (one-hour) time window, helping identify observations that correspond to the same thermal event and reducing duplicate representations.
* FRP Calibration: To make intensity measurements more consistent across sensors, a 1.25x calibration multiplier is applied to MODIS Fire Radiative Power (FRP), aligning its thermal energy scale more closely for comparison alongside VIIRS.
* Risk Estimation & Prediction: Harmonized hotspot data is paired with environmental indicators—such as vegetation conditions (NDVI) and weather factors—to estimate fire risk and generate predictive insights for specific locations.
#### Frontend Experience & Interactive Web Interface
On the frontend, a Flutter web interface presents this information through an interactive, map-driven experience designed for clarity and ease of use. Users can explore interactive map layers showing active hotspots and harmonized results, browse historical fire information, and receive automated, location-based risk insights without having to manually enter complex technical parameters or configure heavy external cloud pipelines.
#### How It Addresses the Challenge & Why It Matters
Working with raw remote-sensing feeds often requires specialized expertise to reconcile multiple satellite products and interpret environmental context. Fire Risk Detector bridges that gap by unifying VIIRS and MODIS detections into a more consistent hotspot dataset while combining thermal monitoring with environmental risk factors inside a single browser workflow.
Why this matters: Having an early, unified view of fire risks supports faster situational awareness, clearer comparisons of fire severity across detections, and more practical decision-making. Whether used for exploration, demonstration, or early risk assessment, turning live satellite and environmental data into an intuitive web interface helps make fire risk information faster to read and easier to act upon.
